_meta.title: Cloud & Container Security
_meta.description: Where the enterprise actually lives now: identity-based attacks on IAM, metadata credential theft, container escape, and serverless abuse. In cloud, identity is the perimeter - and IAM misconfiguration is the new unpatched service.

techniques.name: IAM Privilege Escalation Paths
techniques.summary: AWS-style graphs of forgotten permissions: iam:PassRole + a compute action (run a workload with any role), iam:CreateAccessKey on another user, sts:AssumeRole chains, lambda:UpdateFunctionCode to hijack a privileged function. Rhino's research made these paths computable; Pacu automates them; cloudgoat teaches them hands-on.

detection.description: CloudTrail: CreateAccessKey/CreatePolicyVersion/AssumeRole anomalies per principal, PassRole on unusual compute launches, role assumptions from novel ASNs/regions, GuardDuty privilege-escalation findings, Config drift on IAM policy.
mitigations: Least-privilege IAM with periodic review (IAM Access Analyzer)
Permissions-boundary on every role; deny iam:CreateAccessKey broadly
SCPs blocking high-risk IAM actions outside break-glass roles
CloudTrail enabled org-wide, alerting on the Rhino escalation primitives

techniques.name: Metadata Credential Theft (IMDS Abuse)
techniques.summary: Any code execution on an instance plus SSRF reaches the metadata service and walks away with role credentials - the Capital One breach in one move. IMDSv2 (token via PUT, hop-limit 1) closes the SSRF path; plain IMDSv1 remains open on fleets that never got the memo.

detection.description: VPC flow logs to 169.254.169.254 from non-instance paths, GuardDuty SSRF/ec2 metadata findings, unusual GetRole/GetCredentials on instance profiles, AssumeRole events immediately following app-tier anomalies.
mitigations: IMDSv2 required (HttpTokens=required, hop-limit 1) - fleet-wide, enforced by SCP
Instance-role scope minimal; no admin roles on internet-facing workloads

techniques.name: Container Escape & K8s RBAC Abuse
techniques.summary: Break the boundary: privileged containers (fd access to host devices), hostPath mounts, docker.sock exposure (docker-in-docker is root on the host), kernel primitives, or K8s RBAC paths (pod-create with a privileged spec, service-account token theft, exec into high-priv pods). The crown-jewel jump is always node-level.

detection.description: K8s audit logs: pod-create with privileged/hostPath specs, exec into sensitive namespaces, SA token use from novel IPs; container runtime anomalies (mount of host paths, namespace transitions), eBPF-based runtime security (Falco rules for container breakout patterns).
mitigations: Pod Security Standards (restricted profile), no privileged pods without exception registry
No docker.sock mounts; rootless containers where feasible; seccomp/AppArmor defaults
Least-privilege RBAC per namespace; no default-SA automount for unprivileged workloads
Runtime security (Falco/Tetragon) for syscall-level breakout detection

techniques.name: Serverless & Event-Driven Abuse
techniques.summary: Function code with injection classes (event payloads are user input: S3 keys, headers, queue messages), oversized-bill DoS (recursion, fan-out amplification), event-data poisoning that lands in downstream sinks (the 'serverless SQLi'), and cross-function trust abuse via unwritten event schemas.

detection.description: Function error-rate and invocation anomalies, concurrency spikes near account limits, CloudTrail PutBucketPolicy/CreateAccessKey from function roles, unusual egress from function VPCs, downstream data-store query anomalies correlating with event sources.
mitigations: Treat every event field as untrusted input (validate schemas strictly)
Function-role least privilege; no wildcard actions on data planes
Concurrency caps + budget alerts (the DoS answer is financial, not technical)
Recursion guards and dead-letter queues with alerting
